recommendation: Keep the commit as-is. It is a narrow build-scoped correction to the page linked from the Clinical Reasoning module and directly addresses the stale target-context wording without deciding the other Jira items bundled into the historical SVN 10927 commit.
issue_request: FHIR-11515 was a Published/Persuasive CDS change request requesting clearer ActivityDefinition profiling documentation and clearer explanation of how dynamicValue paths get their target context for medication-style activity definitions.
initial_application: The issue was initially applied in SVN 10927, represented by git commit c03a8aca8404dc242356064fbc17b482dfc33d81, which explicitly included "#11515: Added profiling discussion to ActivityDefinition" and added the Profiling ActivityDefinition section that remains in the current ActivityDefinition notes.
additional_context: ActivityDefinition is active in source/fhir.ini, and the Clinical Reasoning module links the definitional resources topic that contains the medication dynamicValue example. Later source refactors use ActivityDefinition.kind to identify the represented request resource and ActivityDefinition.dosage for medication dosage, while the topic still contained an older category-based fragment and dosageInstruction wording.
reconciliation: Changed source/clinicalreasoning-topics-definitional-resources.html so the medication example declares kind="MedicationRequest" instead of category="drug" and so the nearby prose names ActivityDefinition.dosage. This aligns the current built source with the retained profiling guidance and removes the remaining ambiguity noted by the issue.
source_changes: source/clinicalreasoning-topics-definitional-resources.html: replaced the stale medication example category="drug" fragment with kind="MedicationRequest" and updated prose from dosageInstruction to dosage.
